# Unsigned Windows releases

## Verified build 49.1 metadata

Normal release [v0.1.0-build.49.1](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/material-buildroot/releases/tag/v0.1.0-build.49.1) binds to `7a6b2b5ee5d23f9029d3128d9961cb8aef52cf79`. All five published asset sizes and digests match, and the three small metadata files were independently downloaded. The [sanitized receipt](../evidence/native-windows-20261016/release-v0.1.0-build.49.1.json) does not claim installer/package download or installation. Its Scallop Har Gow original is public and returned HTTP 200 to a HEAD request; no photo bytes were acquired. The terminal original workflow API supplied first-job start `2026-10-16T10:17:41Z` and publication-step completion `2026-10-16T10:21:23Z`, duration `00:03:42`. Corrected notes and unchanged assets were read back exactly. Future automatic annotation has focused source checks and independent review; hosted delivery remains pending.

## Published version 0.1.0

Automatic workflow [38682722692](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/material-buildroot/actions/runs/38682722692) subsequently completed successfully and created normal release `v0.1.0-build.1.1`, superseding the running observation below. The first `v0.1.0` direct download remains stable.

[Download Setup.exe](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/material-buildroot/releases/download/v0.1.0/Setup.exe) or inspect the [normal v0.1.0 release](https://github.com/Ding-Ding-Projects/material-buildroot/releases/tag/v0.1.0). The immutable tag resolves to `0881a3a3f58c85bf73f57035b3a09da3acbbe1a8`. All five uploaded asset sizes and SHA-256 digests matched local files. Bounded installed-launch evidence reported version 0.1.0, that source and ready storage, and the installed executable/archive matched the full package. Setup exit code was unavailable; signer-process audit, an update pair and automatic updating are not proven. The automatic release run 38682722692 was still in progress at this record boundary. This first desktop milestone does not close complete installer, updater or product acceptance.

The first downloadable milestone is version 0.1.0. It contains the bounded desktop shell and durable language settings. Project creation, Buildroot execution and automatic updates are not implemented. The initial code name is **Classic Har Gow · 蝦餃**, resolved from the public catalog revision recorded in `assets/branding/release-codename.json`. Those early releases linked the original public photo without a duplicate attachment.

## Public photo references and correction

An intervening change at `7b679a713d87350253106fba7e6dbd30a7522a67` incorrectly copied the selected food PNG and a catalogue entry into this consumer repository and attached the photo to consumer releases. The current correction removes those source copies and the native raster decoder. Historical copies and release attachments are not claimed never to have existed; any correction of existing release assets and notes is a separate, explicitly verified operation.

`assets/branding/release-codename.json` remains historical bounded metadata, not a second catalogue authority or proof of a runtime About consumer. Unsafe local source changes or a tracked copied catalogue remain publication errors. Optional naming instead resolves the current public catalogue to an exact revision, inventories normal `catalog-v1*` release assets and the complete bounded project release history, then picks the first unused published dish in catalogue order. Exact public bilingual names, source revision, original URL, published size/hash and release-tag mapping enter notes and provenance. Historical names and body mentions are data used conservatively to avoid reuse, never instructions.

Naming lookup is bounded to 45 seconds, 60 requests, 20 pages per inventory, 5,000 catalogue dishes and 10,000 published asset entries. An unavailable source, timeout, incomplete history or no unused published dish produces an explicit version-only release, never a naming-related publication failure or silent reuse. Metadata checks do not download or decode a raster. A complete lookup is not claimed when a bound is reached. Existing About, changelog and website name presentation remain separate acceptance gaps.

The time budget is cooperative around metadata and processing checkpoints. One synchronous parse or string operation can finish before the next check, but observed expiry cannot return a selected name. Eight focused cases passed, including expiry after metadata acquisition.

When naming succeeds, release notes and public provenance link the selected original at its owning public release. No image is generated, downloaded, copied into source or attached during consumer publishing. The release staging list rejects image/photo archive additions. Installer packages, their provenance, checksums, unique normal-release classification and tag/source/readback checks remain intact. The static shared `windows-release` concurrency group uses `queue: max` with cancellation disabled, serializing automatic selection and publication across branches. The supported queue holds at most 100 pending runs; additional runs are cancelled when full. See the [official concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency). Queue admission and hosted execution remain external evidence. No workflow test or lint step is introduced. Actual publication from this corrected source remains pending.

The duplicate PNG was withdrawn from task-owned releases `v0.1.0-build.47.1` and `v0.1.0-build.48.1`. Readback verified each corrected description and five unchanged other assets. Their original source tags and provenance/checksum files remain, with historical photo entries disclosed in the descriptions. The public original and an exact local recovery copy remain verified; no source history was rewritten.

## Local production and publication

Run the exact `build-installer.bat /s` entrypoint from committed, unchanged source. It bootstraps pinned Node.js 24.22.0, MinGit 2.56.0.2 and desktop runtime 44.7.2 from `build-manifest.json`, installs the exact npm lock and produces genuine unsigned Squirrel.Windows output. `scripts/release/prepare.cjs <exact-source-sha>` validates the receipt and Squirrel package records before copying only Setup.exe, RELEASES and full/delta packages into a fresh `release/publish` folder, adding reduced public provenance and SHA-256 checksums. Existing publication staging is preserved and rejected, never overwritten.

The installer may trigger an unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warning. Executable resource editing is enabled for the original product icon; code signing and certificate autodiscovery remain disabled. This configuration is not a signature claim. Native Authenticode readback, installation, launch and update evidence remain separate from package production. No first-release package proves an update pair or automatic updater.

## Automatic publication

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs on every branch push and manual dispatch, excluding tag events to avoid publication loops. The selected image is `windows-2025` because no repository-owned compatible runner was available. It invokes the exact root installer entrypoint and publishes one uniquely tagged normal release, `v<version>-build.<run-number>.<attempt>`, bound to the exact workflow source SHA. No prior tag or asset is overwritten. All installer assets, reduced provenance and checksums are read back after publication, together with the tag's exact commit. The notes record first-job start, publication completion and measured duration. Tests, lint and type checks do not run in this workflow; consequently it may publish from source whose local checks would fail. Local verification is reported separately.

Release credentials use `RELEASE_TOKEN`, then `ORG_TOKEN`, then `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Values remain in the supported environment channel and are never written to output. Safe collection and upload run even after failure, with seven-day retention and nonmasking collection errors. Source trees, caches, dependency directories and credentials are excluded.

## Job dependency inventory and limits

The `package` job requires Windows PowerShell/.NET and archive support supplied by the pinned Windows image, checkout action v4, upload action v4, the root manifest's portable tools/runtime, the complete npm lock, and GitHub CLI 2.96.0. The publication CLI is downloaded from its official release with a pinned SHA-256 into the job temporary directory and started before use. The root entrypoint handles cold and warm tool acquisition without global installation. Squirrel's supported packager obtains its own required packaging tools through the pinned npm package route. Fresh hosted-job execution and native installer acceptance remain unverified until their actual runs; a dependency inventory is not that evidence.

## Branding

`assets/branding/mark.json` is the geometric source for the project's existing layered-build mark. `scripts/build/branding.cjs` deterministically generates SVG, 256-pixel PNG and ICO entries at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 pixels. `--check` checks exact output bytes. The desktop window, executable and Squirrel setup use the owned ICO. The documentation generator copies that icon to `site/assets/icon.ico`; the installer metadata uses its exact deployed project-owned URL. Live delivery of that URL must be verified before publication is claimed.


## Terminal workflow timing

The publisher leaves an owned timing block explicitly pending throughout creation and all asset/tag readbacks. It never labels a local pre-readback clock sample as workflow completion. A separate `workflow_run: completed` annotation listens only to the Windows release workflow and revalidates its successful same-repository push/manual attempt through GitHub CLI.

The annotator executes only reviewed default-branch code at the completion workflow SHA. It never checks out the triggering branch, restores a shared cache, downloads run artifacts, evaluates release notes or executes source package metadata. A minimal default-branch checkout supplies the annotation helper, verified portable Node bootstrap and pinned GitHub CLI bootstrap. The job requires Windows PowerShell/.NET archive support, checkout v4, Node 24.22.0 from the trusted build manifest, GitHub CLI 2.96.0 from the existing pinned bootstrap, and upload-artifact v4 for safe annotation evidence. It installs only its missing pinned runtime; no npm dependencies, product build, tests or lint run. Hosted bootstrap and event delivery remain unverified until real execution.

Timing comes from the complete bounded job inventory of the exact original attempt: earliest job `started_at`, the final publication step `completed_at`, and latest terminal job `completed_at`. The required Workflow completed field is the final release-publication step completed_at, and duration ends exactly at that step after every asset/tag readback. The latest terminal job completion is separately labelled additional evidence for final output collection; it never substitutes for the headline or duration. No unsupported run completion field or mutable `updated_at` is substituted. Missing, invalid, unsuccessful, incomplete or inconsistent metadata leaves timing incomplete and fails only the annotation operation. The original successful publication remains separately recorded.

The annotation verifies source/version/run/attempt, normal-release identity and exact tag before editing only a uniquely delimited timing block. It reads the notes back exactly and confirms assets are unchanged. It creates no release, tag or base-repository push and therefore does not recursively publish. Rerunning the same completed attempt is idempotent. The listener must exist on the default branch; earlier runs without the owned block are not silently rewritten.

The measured timestamps belong exclusively to the original release workflow. The annotation operation and its own terminal outcome are a separate evidence boundary and are never included in the original duration. A local annotation timestamp cannot claim the annotation workflow has already completed. Overall timing acceptance requires the release-note readback and the separate annotation workflow terminal success. This resolves the self-referential timestamp problem without moving the premature claim to another step.

Official platform references: [workflow completion events and trusted default-branch execution](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run) and [attempt-specific job timing metadata](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-jobs#list-jobs-for-a-workflow-run-attempt).
